blocker.prerequisite: A real Terraform refresh-only planner returning exit 0 for this empty persisted-state diff is required for clean acceptance. Exact upstream cause is not established; no owner API or runtime drift was observed.

verification.source_changes: Fixture only; no CodeBuild Go owner bug observed and no shared source, root build, staging or commit performed.

prerequisites: A prebuilt actual controller selected with --stackd; this runner does not build or replace shared/root source.
Python and examples/requirements.txt; Terraform 1.15.9 on PATH; provider AWS 6.68.0 installed from publisher or a prepared filesystem mirror.
No AWS account, paid cloud resource, inherited AWS credentials, external endpoint or existing controller is used.

Default mode needs no container runtime: Step Functions activity callbacks and S3 pipeline deployment are actual consumers. CodeBuild projects in this mode are lifecycle controls only, not successful jobs.

Docker mode requires explicit local Docker Engine transport, trusted dedicated host, reachable compute endpoint selected by examples/local.py containers=True, and an installed immutable Linux build image containing /bin/sh and python3 on PATH. Prepare the image yourself; the fixture never pulls images or installs packages.

Controller, SQLite DB, Terraform state/plans, outputs and evidence live in a unique mode-0700 retained workspace. --work-parent selects an existing parent; --stackd selects a prebuilt executable; --port must be unused.
consumers: Signed Step Functions SDK StartExecution against alias, unqualified machine and retained old published version; actual activity lease/input, worker SHA-256 computation, heartbeat, task-token success, terminal output and retained ActivitySucceeded history.

Signed SDK StartPipelineExecution; independent S3 reads of retained source/output ZIPs and deployed binary member bytes. Default mode is S3 Source -> S3 Deploy; Docker mode is S3 Source -> real CodeBuild -> S3 Deploy.
Docker mode additionally starts an independent NO_SOURCE CodeBuild process, awaits its real completion and consumes its S3 ZIP artifact's process-produced binary bytes.

v1 -> v2 changes project description/environment/tags/concurrency, pipeline destination prefix/tags, machine definition/publication, activity tags, alias description/routes. The original v1 workflow version is executed after v2 is current.

After a real controller stop and SQLite reopen, independently read retained successful workflow histories, pipeline ZIP and deployment bytes, and (Docker mode) actual build history and BUILD_ID-namespaced artifact bytes; then start fresh alias, unqualified and retained-version workflows, a fresh pipeline, and a fresh standalone build in Docker mode.

Private evidence.json records factual stages, owned identities, Terraform command exit codes/log paths, consumer execution handles and artifact hashes, and ordinary destroy/signed absence/empty-state cleanup.
not_covered: Fleet, source credentials, report groups, CodeBuild resource policies or webhooks, CodePipeline custom action types or webhooks.
Provider actions and list-resource query interfaces are inventoried separately but not exercised by this lifecycle fixture.
No claim of whole-service parity, every supported setting, batch/agent readiness, cryptographic substitution or successful jobs without actual runtime execution.

resources.import: project ARN (provider also resolves a name via BatchGetProjects)
resources.fix: UpdateProject concurrentBuildLimit=-1 now removes the retained per-project limit instead of failing positive-limit validation; provider emits this sentinel when concurrent_build_limit is removed.
gaps: UpdateProjectVisibility is not registered: PUBLIC project visibility and resource_access_role changes are unsupported.
Badges, nonzero auto_retry_limit, build_batch_config, file_system_locations and VPC projects reject as unimplemented.
Only LINUX_CONTAINER and BUILD_GENERAL1_SMALL/MEDIUM/LARGE compute are admitted; other platforms, architectures/compute types, Lambda compute and Mac/Windows environments are unsupported.
Privileged mode, custom certificates, compute_configuration, docker_server and host_kernel are unsupported.

CODECOMMIT source, build-status reporting, insecure TLS and primary source identifiers are unsupported. Supported Git providers still require actual authorized reachable Git servers; this fixture does not supply Git credentials.

LOCAL cache and local cache modes reject; only S3 and NO_CACHE are supported. S3 cache/logging, secret/parameter environment values, secondary sources/artifacts and registry credentials are outside this fixture.
Non-NONE artifact bucket_owner_access rejects; fleet-backed projects need real ACTIVE capacity from the independent fleet runtime.

resources.import: fleet ARN including native incarnation UUID
gaps: Creation requires configured real FleetExecutor and installed immutable -codebuild-fleet-image, not fabricated ACTIVE status.
Only LINUX_CONTAINER, BUILD_GENERAL1_SMALL/MEDIUM/LARGE, positive base capacity, QUEUE/ON_DEMAND overflow, tags and optional validated service role are admitted.
Custom AMI/image_id, compute_configuration, proxy_configuration, scaling_configuration and VPC configurations reject.
Capacity/compute/environment/service-role/image changes are unsupported; update only accepts unchanged capacity settings plus overflow behavior and tags. No resize/drain implementation is claimed.
Fixture does not create/import/update/destroy a fleet or exercise fleet data source.
Report-group lifecycle, report ingestion/export and report byte consumers have no registered CodeBuild owner operations.
These API operations are not registered. Existing RAM-backed resource sharing does not implement this Terraform resource.

resources.import: credential ARN; token itself cannot be recovered from list
gaps: Needs configured actual credential cipher and real provider credentials for an authenticated Git consumer; no fake token fixture is supplied.
PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN, SECRETS_MANAGER and BITBUCKET BASIC_AUTH are admitted. OAUTH is console-only and other auth modes reject. BASIC_AUTH/username are valid only for BITBUCKET.
Supported server types are GITHUB, GITHUB_ENTERPRISE, BITBUCKET, GITLAB and GITLAB_SELF_MANAGED; this fixture does not establish live Git provider authorization or push/webhook delivery.
CreateWebhook, UpdateWebhook and DeleteWebhook are unregistered; no real source-provider hook provisioning, authentication or delivery owner is present.

settings_supported_by_fixture: CodeBuild Build in Docker opt-in mode
gaps: Cross-region artifact_stores and triggers reject. Cross-account/cross-region action roles are not claimed.
Automatic stage before_entry/on_success/on_failure conditions, rule execution, automatic rollback and stage blockers are unsupported.

Only AWS S3 Source/Deploy, CodeBuild Build/Test, AppConfig Deploy, Manual Approval and Lambda Invoke action families have real owners. GitHub/CodeStar/CodeCommit/ECS/CloudFormation/other providers and custom/third-party workers are unsupported.
CodeBuild batch actions and action command/environment declarations are unsupported; provider-specific broad quotas/error-precedence are not complete.
Pipeline definition updates fence old advancement but do not establish natural terminal cancellation of old pending work; fixture finishes admitted work before changing configuration.
Custom action-type lifecycle and custom/third-party worker job acquisition are unimplemented; built-in provider execution does not establish custom action support.
Webhook lifecycle, real external hook registration and authenticated ingress delivery are not registered owner operations.
Fixture uses AWS-owned encryption only; customer-managed encryption requires actual KMS owner/key authority and is not exercised here.
Activity name changes are replacement, not an update API; only tags are updated in place.
Two-version weighted routing is implemented but not exercised; this fixture makes no statistical distribution claim.
Alias automatic deployment strategies/alarms are not fields of this pinned Terraform resource and are not implied by route updates.
There is no separate aws_sfn_state_machine_version resource in service_package_gen.go: published versions belong to state_machine.publish and are observed by the versions data source and SDK.
version_description is provider-computed-only in AWS 6.68.0, not a configurable publication description.

Fixture does not exercise EXPRESS, logging_configuration, tracing_configuration, customer-managed encryption_configuration, distributed Map, ECS/Lambda integrations, nested workflows, JSONata, retries or redrive. These have existing owners with their documented boundaries, not blanket fixture coverage.
Arbitrary AWS SDK integrations require their real target service owner and current execution-role authority; operation selection alone is not whole-service execution parity.
No fake process invocation or activity completion is used: the explicit Python SDK worker owns the leased task result.
Needs an independently created real fleet with a configured reservation image/runtime; fixture supplies no fake fleet.
Name lookup is exercised; direct ARN lookup is implemented but not separately exercised.
Single alias in owned scope; provider's first-page/suffix-match lookup behavior is not broad alias pagination conformance.
Name lookup and current definition are exercised; multi-page/multi-region account discovery is not.
Two retained publications exercised before and after SQLite reopen; 1000-version quotas and multi-page enumeration are not exercised.
Runner invokes actual StartBuild through SDK in Docker mode, not Terraform action syntax.
